questions.question: Identify the missing link: Scarcity, Demand, Supply, ________
questions.solution:

•

• 
 
**Supply:** This represents how much of that resource producers are willing to provide.

 
 
•

questions.question: How many 4-letter words (without repetition) can you make using D, E, A, L?
questions.solution:
**Given:** Letters = {D, E, A, L}, n = 4

**Formula Used:** Number of permutations of n distinct objects taken all at a time = n!

⇒ Number of ways to fill the first position = 4 (D, E, A, or L)

⇒ Number of ways to fill the second position = 3 (remaining letters)

⇒ Number of ways to fill the third position = 2 (remaining letters)

⇒ Number of ways to fill the fourth position = 1 (last letter)

⇒ Total 4-letter words = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1

⇒ Total words = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

questions.question: What is the term for the movement of tectonic plates causing earthquakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plate tectonics**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plate tectonics** is the scientific theory that describes the large-scale motion of the seven large plates and the movements of a larger number of smaller plates of Earth's **lithosphere**.
 
• Earthquakes occur when these tectonic plates interact at their boundaries. The friction between the plates causes **stress** to build up; when this stress is suddenly released, it sends **seismic waves** through the Earth's crust, resulting in an earthquake.
 
• **Erosion** is a geological process in which earthen materials are worn away and transported by natural forces such as wind or water, which does not cause tectonic earthquakes.
 
• **Sedimentation** is the tendency for particles in suspension to settle out of the fluid in which they are entrained and come to rest against a barrier, a process unrelated to plate movement.
 
• **Convection** (specifically mantle convection) is the slow creeping motion of Earth's solid silicate mantle caused by convection currents carrying heat from the interior to the surface. While it is the **driving force** behind plate movement, the movement itself and the resulting earthquakes are categorized under the theory of **Plate tectonics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The theory of plate tectonics built upon the concept of **Continental Drift**, an idea first proposed by scientist **Alfred Wegener** in 1912.
 
• There are three primary types of plate boundaries: **Divergent** (moving apart), **Convergent** (moving together), and **Transform** (sliding past each other).
 
• Most of the world's earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur along the **Pacific Ring of Fire**, which is a direct result of plate tectonics and the movement of several major and minor tectonic plates.
 
• The point inside the Earth where the earthquake starts is called the **Hypocenter** (or focus), and the point directly above it on the surface is the **Epicenter**.

questions.question: What term describes animals that regulate their body temperatures internally?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Endotherms**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Endotherms** are animals that primarily produce their own heat through **metabolic processes** to maintain a stable internal body temperature, regardless of the external environment.

• These animals are often referred to as **warm-blooded**. Common examples include **birds** and **mammals**.

• **Ectotherms** (Option 1) are animals that rely on external environmental sources, such as sunlight or heated rock surfaces, to regulate their body temperature. They are often called **cold-blooded** animals, like reptiles and fish.

• **Amphibians** (Option 3) are a class of cold-blooded vertebrates that spend part of their lives in water and part on land. While they are ectothermic, the term refers to their biological class rather than the specific mechanism of heat regulation.

• **Invertebrates** (Option 4) are animals that do not possess a **backbone** or vertebral column. While most invertebrates are ectothermic, the term describes their skeletal structure.

**Additional Information__**

• The process of maintaining a steady internal state is known as **Homeostasis**.

• **Endothermy** allows animals to remain active in cooler environments and during the night, but it requires a much higher **caloric intake** compared to ectotherms because generating heat is energy-intensive.

• Some animals exhibit **Poikilothermy**, where their internal temperature varies considerably, usually as a result of the variation in the ambient temperature.

• **Thermoregulation** strategies include physiological changes (like sweating or shivering) and behavioral changes (like seeking shade or huddling).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the relationship between velocity and acceleration in different dimensions?

options.text: In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration are always perpendicular to each other.
In two-dimensional motion, acceleration must always act opposite to velocity.
In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration lie along the same line, either in the same or opposite direction.
In three-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration must always act in the same direction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In one-dimensional motion, velocity and acceleration lie along the same line, either in the same or opposite direction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__

• **One-dimensional motion**, also known as **rectilinear motion**, refers to movement along a straight line. In this case, the position of the object can be described using a single coordinate (e.g., x).

• The **velocity** vector always points in the direction of motion along that straight line.

• **Acceleration** is defined as the rate of change of velocity. For the motion to remain strictly one-dimensional, any change in the velocity must occur along the same axis. Therefore, acceleration must act along the same line as velocity.

• If **velocity and acceleration** are in the **same direction**, the object is **speeding up**.

• If **velocity and acceleration** are in **opposite directions**, the object is **slowing down** (also known as **deceleration** or **retardation**).

• In **two-dimensional** or **three-dimensional** motion, acceleration can be at any angle to the velocity vector, which allows the object to change its **direction** of motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In **Uniform Circular Motion**, the acceleration (centripetal acceleration) is always **perpendicular** to the velocity vector. This changes the direction of the object but not its speed.

• In **Projectile Motion** (a type of 2D motion), the acceleration due to gravity is constant and acts vertically downwards, while the velocity has both horizontal and vertical components.

• **Instantaneous velocity** is the derivative of position with respect to time, and **instantaneous acceleration** is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.

• If acceleration is **zero**, the velocity remains **constant** in both magnitude and direction.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following best illustrates a liquidity trap?

options.text: The central bank raises interest rates to control inflation.
Commercial banks stop lending due to high default risks.
Interest rates are near zero, but people prefer holding cash instead of investing.
The government increases taxes to reduce fiscal deficit.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interest rates are near zero, but people prefer holding cash instead of investing.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• A **liquidity trap** is an economic situation where **monetary policy** becomes ineffective because **nominal interest rates** are at or near **zero**, and consumers and investors prefer to hoard **cash** rather than invest in **bonds** or other debt instruments.

• In this state, the **demand for money** becomes **perfectly elastic**. This means that any increase in the **money supply** by the **Central Bank** (such as the **RBI** in India or the **Federal Reserve** in the US) does not result in a further drop in interest rates or an increase in **aggregate demand**.

• The core logic involves the **speculative demand for money**. When interest rates are exceptionally low, people expect them to rise in the **future**. Since **bond prices** have an inverse relationship with interest rates, a future rise in rates would lead to a **capital loss** on bonds, making cash a safer asset to hold.

• **Statement 1** describes **Contractionary Monetary Policy**, which is used by a central bank to reduce **inflation** by increasing the **cost of borrowing**. This is the opposite of the conditions leading to a liquidity trap. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 2** refers to a **Credit Crunch**. While this involves a lack of lending, it is driven by **bank insolvency** or **risk aversion** among lenders rather than the public's preference for cash due to low interest rates. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 3** accurately illustrates the **liquidity trap** where the **opportunity cost** of holding cash is nearly zero, leading to a preference for **liquidity** over **investment**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

• **Statement 4** describes **Fiscal Consolidation** or **Austerity** measures. While this affects the **economy**, it is a **fiscal policy** tool and does not define the monetary phenomenon of a liquidity trap. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

__

• **Keynesian Origin**: The concept was first proposed by the British economist **John Maynard Keynes** in his seminal work, **The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money**, published in **1936**. He argued that in such times, the economy is in a **depression** that cannot be cured by monetary means alone.

• **The IS-LM Model**: In macroeconomic theory, a liquidity trap is represented by a **horizontal LM curve**. In this range, shifting the **LM curve** to the right through **monetary expansion** fails to increase the **National Income (GDP)** or lower the **interest rate**.

• **Deflationary Expectations**: Often, a liquidity trap is accompanied by **deflation** (a general decrease in prices). If people expect prices to fall, the **real interest rate** (nominal rate minus inflation) remains high even if the **nominal rate** is **0%**, further discouraging **consumption** and **investment**.

• **Policy Alternatives**: When a country falls into this trap, economists suggest that **Expansionary Fiscal Policy**—where the **government** increases **public spending** or cuts **taxes**—is the most effective way to stimulate **Aggregate Demand**.

• **Historical Examples**: **Japan** is the most famous modern example, having faced a liquidity trap during its **Lost Decade** in the **1990s**. More recently, many developed nations experienced similar conditions following the **Global Financial Crisis of 2008** and the **COVID-19 pandemic** in **2020**.

**Important Points__**

• **Zero Lower Bound (ZLB)**: This is the limitation where **nominal interest rates** cannot practically go below zero. Once the **Central Bank** reaches this limit, traditional **monetary policy** tools (like lowering the **Repo Rate**) lose their power.

• **Quantitative Easing (QE)**: To bypass a liquidity trap, central banks may use **unconventional monetary policy** like **Quantitative Easing**. This involves the large-scale purchase of **long-term government bonds** and other **financial assets** to inject **liquidity** directly into the **financial system**.

• **Savings Paradox**: During a liquidity trap, the **Paradox of Thrift** often occurs. As individuals try to save more to protect themselves during an **economic downturn**, **total savings** in the economy may actually fall because the decrease in **consumption** leads to lower **total income**.

• **Role of Expectations**: The trap is largely driven by **psychology**. If the public does not believe that the **economy** will improve or that **inflation** will return, they will continue to hold **cash**, keeping the **velocity of money** extremely low.

5b

This statement is **correct** as the **Copper Hoard** implements, including **harpoons**, **celts**, and **swords**, have been found in the same archaeological layers as **Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP)**. **Hence, Reason (R) is true.**

• The presence of **mud structures**, **post-holes**, and **wattle-and-daub** walls at sites like **Lal Qila** and **Saipai** confirms that these people lived in permanent or semi-permanent settlements in the **Upper Gangetic Valley**.

questions.question: What is the key focus of NRLM (National Rural Livelihood Mission)?
questions.solution:

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)** was launched by the **Ministry of Rural Development**, **Government of India**, in **June 2011**. It was later renamed **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana (DAY-NRLM)** in **November 2015**.

• The key focus and core strategy of the mission is the **Formation of Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**. • The scheme does not focus on **Providing free food grains**. This is the primary objective of the **National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013**, and the **Public Distribution System (PDS)**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***

• **Building rural roads** is the specific mandate of the **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**, which was launched in **December 2000** to provide all-weather road connectivity to unconnected habitations. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

• **Promoting urban employment** is the goal of the **National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM)**. **NRLM** is strictly dedicated to the **rural** population and poverty alleviation in villages. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

• The mission follows a **demand-driven strategy**, where states have the flexibility to develop their own **poverty reduction action plans** based on local needs.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Universal Social Mobilization**: The mission seeks to bring at least **one woman member** from each identified rural poor household into the **Self-Help Group (SHG)** network in a time-bound manner.

• **Financial Inclusion**: **DAY-NRLM** works on both the demand and supply sides of financial inclusion. It provides **Revolving Funds (RF)** and **Community Investment Funds (CIF)** to SHGs to strengthen their financial base and encourage internal lending.

• **Interest Subvention**: The mission provides interest subvention to SHGs to ensure they can access bank credit at an effective interest rate of **7% per annum**. In **250 identified backward districts**, an additional subvention of **3%** is provided for prompt repayment, reducing the effective rate to **4%**.

• **Livelihood Enhancement**: It focuses on stabilizing and promoting existing livelihoods of the poor through **agriculture**, **non-farm sectors**, and **skill development**.

• **Funding Pattern**: It is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** where the funding is shared between the **Centre** and the **States** in the ratio of **60:40** (for general states) and **90:10** (for North-Eastern and Himalayan states).

• **Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP)**: A sub-component of **NRLM**, it aims to empower women in agriculture by making systematic investments to enhance their participation and productivity.

• **Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana (AGEY)**: Launched in **2017**, it provides alternative livelihood options to SHG members by allowing them to operate **public transport services** in backward rural areas.

</ul

• **Holi** is the **Festival of Colors**, celebrated to mark the arrival of spring and the victory of **Prahlada** over the demoness **Holika**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• **Navratri** is a festival spanning **nine nights** dedicated to the worship of **Goddess Durga** and her nine different forms. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

• The return of **Lord Rama** to **Ayodhya** is celebrated by lighting thousands of **earthen lamps** (**diyas**), symbolizing the victory of **light over darkness** and **good over evil**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Diwali** is observed on the **Amavasya** (new moon day) of the month of **Kartik** in the **Hindu Lunisolar calendar**, which usually falls in **October** or **November**.

• The festival is a **five-day** celebration that begins with **Dhanteras**, followed by **Naraka Chaturdashi** (**Chhoti Diwali**), **Lakshmi Puja**, **Govardhan Puja**, and ends with **Bhai Dooj**.

• In **Sikhism**, the day is celebrated as **Bandi Chhor Divas** to commemorate the release of **Guru Hargobind Ji**, the **sixth Sikh Guru**, from the **Gwalior Fort** in **1619**.

• In **West Bengal** and **Odisha**, the day is also celebrated as **Kali Puja** to honor **Goddess Kali**, the destroyer of evil.

**Important Points__**

• The life and journey of **Lord Rama** are detailed in the ancient Indian epic **Ramayana**, composed by **Sage Valmiki**.

• **Ayodhya**, the birthplace of **Lord Rama**, is located on the banks of the **Saryu River** in the state of **Uttar Pradesh**, **India**.

• During the festival, people decorate their homes with **Rangoli** (artistic floor patterns) and prepare various **sweets** to share with friends and family.

• **Goddess Lakshmi**, the deity of **wealth** and **prosperity**, and **Lord Ganesha**, the remover of obstacles, are the primary deities worshipped during **Lakshmi Puja**.

</ul

questions.question: The Gothic architectural style originated in which continent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Europe**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Gothic architectural style** originated in the continent of **Europe**, specifically in **France**, during the **mid-12th century**. It remained the dominant architectural language for religious and secular buildings until the **16th century**.

• The style evolved from **Romanesque architecture** and is characterized by its move toward greater height, light, and structural efficiency. The transition was marked by the reconstruction of the **Abbey Church of Saint-Denis** near **Paris**, initiated by **Abbot Suger** in **1140**.

• The core innovation of the **Gothic style** was the **pointed arch**. Unlike the rounded arches of the **Romanesque** period, the pointed arch allowed for the weight of the roof to be directed more vertically, enabling the construction of much taller walls.

• Other defining features include the **ribbed vault** and the **flying buttress**. These structural elements allowed architects to create thinner walls and incorporate massive **stained-glass windows**, filling the interiors with light, which was a significant departure from the dark, heavy interiors of earlier styles.

• From **France**, the style spread rapidly across the **European** continent, reaching **England**, **Germany**, **Spain**, **Italy**, and **Central Europe**, with each region developing its own unique variations, such as **Perpendicular Gothic** in **England** or **Sondergotik** in **Germany**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Etymology**: The term **Gothic** was originally used as a derogatory label by **Renaissance** writers like **Giorgio Vasari**. They associated the style with the **Goths**, a Germanic tribe that had invaded the **Roman Empire**, viewing the medieval style as barbaric compared to classical **Greek** and **Roman** standards.

• **Structural Components**: The **flying buttress** is perhaps the most iconic feature. It is an external masonry structure that resists the lateral thrust of a roof or vault. This allowed for the creation of the **Clerestory**, the upper part of the nave containing windows that let in direct sunlight.

• **Artistic Elements**: **Gothic** cathedrals are famous for their **Rose Windows**, which are large, circular stained-glass windows typically found at the ends of the transepts or the west facade. These windows often depicted complex theological narratives through **stained glass**.

• **Famous Examples**: Some of the most renowned **Gothic** structures in **Europe** include **Notre-Dame de Paris** (France), **Chartres Cathedral** (France), **Westminster Abbey** (England), **Cologne Cathedral** (Germany), and **Milan Cathedral** (Italy).

• **Gothic Revival**: In the **18th** and **19th centuries**, a movement known as **Neo-Gothic** or **Gothic Revival** emerged. This movement sought to revive medieval **Gothic** forms and was used extensively in the design of university campuses, government buildings (like the **Palace of Westminster** in **London**), and churches across the world.

• **UNESCO Recognition**: Many of these **European** cathedrals are now protected as **UNESCO World Heritage Sites**, recognized for their **architectural** genius and their role as centers of **medieval** culture and learning.
</ul

questions.question: When is a 'Vote on Account' necessary?

options.text: To ensure continuity of government operations until the budget is passed

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To ensure continuity of government operations until the budget is passed**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Article 116** of the **Constitution of India** provides for a **Vote on Account**, which is a grant in advance made by the **Parliament** to the **Executive**.

• The primary purpose of a **Vote on Account** is to ensure the **continuity of government operations**. Since the **financial year** begins on **April 1st** and the **Budget** (the **Annual Financial Statement**) usually takes a few months to be debated and passed, the government needs funds to cover its essential **expenditure** during this transition period. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***

• It serves as a temporary authorization to withdraw money from the **Consolidated Fund of India**. Without this, the government would legally be unable to spend money after **March 31st**, leading to a shutdown of public services.

• A **Vote on Account** does not deal with **new taxation policies**. Changes in taxes are proposed through the **Finance Bill** as part of the regular budget process. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• It is not a tool used to **reduce fiscal deficit**. Fiscal deficit management involves long-term policy decisions, **expenditure** control, and **revenue** generation strategies, often guided by the **FRBM Act, 2003**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Supplementary grants** are governed by **Article 115** and are sought when the amount authorized for a specific service in the **Appropriation Act** for the current **financial year** is found to be insufficient. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Duration and Amount**: By convention, a **Vote on Account** is usually passed for a period of **two months**. The amount granted is typically **one-sixth (1/6th)** of the total estimated **expenditure** presented in the **Budget** for the entire **financial year**.

• **Interim Budget vs. Vote on Account**: While a **Vote on Account** only deals with the **expenditure** side of the government's ledger, an **Interim Budget** (presented during an **election year**) includes both **expenditure** and **receipts** (revenue) estimates.

• **Consolidated Fund of India**: Defined under **Article 266**, this fund contains all **revenues** received by the government, **loans** raised, and **money** received in repayment of loans. No amount can be withdrawn from it without an **Appropriation Act** passed by the **Parliament**.

• **Appropriation Bill**: Under **Article 114**, the **Appropriation Bill** is introduced in the **Lok Sabha** after the **demands for grants** are voted upon. It gives legal authority to the government to withdraw funds from the **Consolidated Fund**.

• **Shift in Budget Date**: Since **2017**, the **Union Budget** has been presented on **February 1st** instead of the last day of February. This change was implemented to complete the legislative process before the start of the new **financial year** on **April 1st**, thereby minimizing the need for a **Vote on Account** in normal years.

**Important Points__**

• **Exclusive Power of Lok Sabha**: The **Vote on Account** is a special provision where the **Lok Sabha** can pass the grant without a full-scale discussion, ensuring that the **administrative machinery** does not come to a halt.

• **No Policy Changes**: It is a formal convention that the government does not announce major **policy changes** or **new schemes** during a **Vote on Account** or an **Interim Budget**, leaving such decisions to the **new government** formed after **elections**.

• **Constitutional Requirement**: **Article 265** states that no **tax** shall be levied or collected except by **authority of law**, and **Article 266** ensures **Parliamentary control** over **expenditure**, making the **Vote on Account** a vital constitutional mechanism for **fiscal accountability**.
</ul

questions.question: Name the situation when the central bank reduces interest rates to stimulate economic growth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expansionary monetary policy**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Expansionary monetary policy** is a macroeconomic strategy used by a **central bank** (like the **Reserve Bank of India** or the **Federal Reserve**) to stimulate the economy by increasing the **money supply**. This is primarily achieved by **reducing interest rates**, which makes borrowing cheaper for consumers and businesses. ***Hence, the correct answer is Expansionary monetary policy.***

• When the **central bank** lowers the **policy rates** (such as the **Repo Rate**), commercial banks typically lower their lending rates. This encourages **investment** and **consumption**, leading to higher **aggregate demand** and **economic growth**.

• **Contractionary monetary policy** is the opposite of expansionary policy. It involves **increasing interest rates** to reduce the money supply and slow down economic activity, usually to combat high **inflation**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Fiscal stimulus** refers to measures taken by the **government**, such as increasing **public spending** or reducing **taxes**, to boost the economy. While it aims for growth, it is a tool of **fiscal policy**, not monetary policy managed by a central bank. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Quantitative easing** is an unconventional monetary policy where a central bank purchases **government bonds** or other financial assets from the market to inject **liquidity** directly into the economy. While it is expansionary in nature, the specific action of reducing interest rates is the standard definition of expansionary monetary policy. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**: In **India**, the **MPC** is responsible for fixing the benchmark interest rate (**Repo Rate**). It consists of **6 members**, including the **Governor of the RBI**, and meets at least **4 times a year**.

• **Repo Rate**: This is the rate at which the **Reserve Bank of India** lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds. It is a key tool used to control **inflation** and **liquidity**.

• **Reverse Repo Rate**: This is the rate at which the **RBI** borrows money from commercial banks within the country. It helps the central bank to absorb excess **liquidity** from the banking system.

• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**: This is a specific share of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that banks must keep with the **RBI** in the form of **cash**. Increasing the **CRR** is a contractionary measure, while decreasing it is expansionary.

• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**: This is the minimum percentage of deposits that a commercial bank has to maintain in the form of **liquid cash**, **gold**, or other **securities** before providing credit to customers.

**Important Points__**

• The primary objective of **monetary policy** in **India** is to maintain **price stability** while keeping in mind the objective of **growth**. The **RBI Act, 1934** was amended in **2016** to provide a statutory basis for the implementation of the flexible **inflation targeting** framework.

• The current **inflation target** set by the **Government of India** is **4%** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%** (i.e., a range of **2% to 6%**).

• **Open Market Operations (OMO)**: These involve the simultaneous **purchase and sale** of **government securities** by the **RBI** to regulate the **money supply** in the economy over the long term.

• **Bank Rate**: It is the rate at which the **RBI** is ready to buy or rediscount bills of exchange or other commercial papers. It is also known as the **Discount Rate**.
</ul

questions.question: Which region of the world has the highest elderly dependency ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Europe**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **elderly dependency ratio** is a demographic measure that represents the number of elderly people (typically those aged **65 years and older**) per **100 individuals** of working age (usually **15 to 64 years**). It indicates the potential burden on the working population to support the non-working elderly population.

• **Europe** is the region with the highest elderly dependency ratio in the world. This is a result of the region being in the advanced stages of the **Demographic Transition Model**, characterized by **low birth rates** and **high life expectancy**.

• According to data from the **United Nations Population Division**, European countries such as **Italy**, **Germany**, **Greece**, and **Portugal** have some of the highest proportions of elderly citizens globally. In these nations, the number of retirees is growing faster than the number of new workers entering the labor force.

• In contrast, **Africa** has the lowest elderly dependency ratio. This is because the continent has a very young population structure with high **fertility rates**, meaning the proportion of people over **65** is relatively small compared to the large youth and working-age population.

• While **Asia** (specifically countries like **Japan** and **South Korea**) and **South America** are seeing rapid increases in their elderly populations, the continental average for **Europe** remains the highest due to decades of sustained low fertility and medical advancements that have increased **longevity**.

**Additional Information__**

__

• The **Demographic Transition Model (DTM)** describes the transition from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as a country develops. Most European nations are in **Stage 4** or **Stage 5**, where the population begins to age significantly or even decline.

• A high elderly dependency ratio poses significant **economic challenges**, including increased pressure on **pension systems**, higher **healthcare costs** for geriatric care, and a potential shortage of labor in the **productive sectors** of the economy.

• **Japan**, although located in **Asia**, is the individual country with the highest elderly dependency ratio in the world, with over **28%** of its population aged **65 or older** as of recent **World Bank** data.

• To mitigate the effects of an aging population, many countries in **Europe** are implementing policies such as **increasing the retirement age**, encouraging **skilled immigration**, and providing **pro-natalist incentives** to boost birth rates.

• The **World Population Prospects 2022** report highlights that the global population is aging at an unprecedented rate. By the **year 2050**, the number of persons aged **65 years or over** globally is projected to be more than twice the number of children under age **5**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Old-Age Dependency Ratio (OADR)** is specifically used by **economists** and **policymakers** to calculate the **sustainability** of **social security** benefits. A ratio of **1:3**, for example, means there are three working-age people for every one elderly person.

• **Sub-Saharan Africa** remains the 'youngest' region, where the **child dependency ratio** (0-14 years) is the primary demographic concern rather than the elderly ratio.

• **Silver Economy** is a term used to describe the economic opportunities and markets that emerge from the needs of the aging population, particularly in sectors like **biotechnology**, **home-care services**, and **leisure**.

• The **United Nations** designates **October 1st** as the **International Day of Older Persons** to raise awareness about the opportunities and challenges of aging in the **21st century**.
</ul

questions.question: Name the state known as the 'Oil Bowl of India' due to abundant crude oil production?

• The first commercial discovery of **crude oil** in **India** occurred at **Digboi** in the **Tinsukia district** of **Assam** in the year **1889**. Following this discovery, the **Digboi Oil Refinery** was commissioned in **1901**, which remains the **oldest operating refinery** in the world.

• The major oil-bearing strata in **Assam** are located in the **Brahmaputra Valley**. Significant oil fields include **Digboi**, **Naharkatiya** (discovered in **1953**), and **Moran-Hugrijan** (discovered in **1956**), which have been contributing to the **nation's** energy security for decades.

• The term **Oil Bowl** is attributed to the state due to the high concentration of **hydrocarbon** reserves and the density of **oil wells** and **refineries** within the **Upper Assam**

questions.question: Alauddin Khilji's reign is marked by his successful defense against which foreign invader?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mongols**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji**, who ruled the **Delhi Sultanate** from **1296 to 1316**, is celebrated in history for his successful defense of India against the **Mongol** invasions. The **Mongols** of the **Chagatai Khanate** launched several large-scale attacks during his reign, aiming to conquer the heart of North India.
 
• The major **Mongol** invasions occurred in **1297-98**, **1299**, **1303**, and **1305**. Unlike his predecessors, **Alauddin Khilji** adopted a proactive military stance, defeating the **Mongol** forces in battles such as the **Battle of Jalandhar (1298)** and the **Battle of Kili (1299)**. **Hence, the option Mongols is correct.**
 
• To protect the capital, **Delhi**, from **Mongol** raids, he constructed the **Siri Fort** around **1303**. This fort served as a massive defensive garrison and the second city of **Delhi**.
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** implemented rigorous military reforms to sustain a large army. He introduced the **Dagh** system (branding of horses) and the **Chehra** system (descriptive rolls of soldiers) to ensure the quality and loyalty of his troops.
 
• His **Market Control Policy** or **Price Control Measures** were specifically designed to keep the cost of living low, enabling him to maintain a massive standing army with relatively low salaries, which was essential for the continuous defense against **Mongol** threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Timur (Tamerlane)**: He was a **Turco-Mongol** conqueror who invaded India much later, in the year **1398**. His invasion took place during the reign of **Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq** of the **Tughlaq Dynasty**. **Timur** sacked **Delhi**, causing widespread destruction, but this was long after **Alauddin Khilji** had died. **Hence, the option Timur is incorrect.**
 
• **Babur**: He was the founder of the **Mughal Empire** in India. **Babur** invaded India in the **16th century** and defeated **Ibrahim Lodi** in the **First Battle of Panipat** in **1526**. His era is distinct from the **Khilji** period by over two centuries. **Hence, the option Babur is incorrect.**
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni**: He was the ruler of the **Ghaznavid Empire** who conducted **17 raids** into India between **1000 and 1027 AD**. His primary motive was to plunder the wealth of Indian temples, such as the **Somnath Temple** in **1025 AD**. He predates the **Khilji Dynasty** by nearly 300 years. **Hence, the option Mahmud of Ghazni is incorrect.**
 
• **Khilji Dynasty**: It was the second dynasty to rule the **Delhi Sultanate**, founded by **Jalal-ud-din Firuz Khilji** in **1290**. **Alauddin Khilji** was the most powerful ruler of this dynasty, known for his administrative reforms and territorial expansions into **South India** under his general **Malik Kafur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Zafar Khan**: He was one of **Alauddin Khilji**'s most valiant generals who played a crucial role in repelling the **Mongols**. He died heroically in the **Battle of Kili** in **1299** while fighting the forces of **Qutlugh Khwaja**.
 
• **Administrative Centralization**: To prevent internal rebellions while focusing on external **Mongol** threats, **Alauddin** prohibited the social gatherings of nobles and banned the use of wine and intoxicants.
 
• **Revenue Reforms**: He was the first Sultan to insist that in the **Doab** region, land revenue should be assessed on the basis of measuring the land (**Paimash**). This ensured a steady flow of income to the state to fund the military.
 
• **Economic Impact**: His strict enforcement of prices for grains, cloth, and other necessities ensured that even during **Mongol** sieges, the supply chain and economic stability of **Delhi** remained intact.

questions.question: How many schedules are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India** currently consists of **12 schedules**. These schedules are essentially supplementary tables that provide detailed information regarding various articles of the **Constitution**.
 
• At the time of its **adoption** on **26 November 1949** and its **commencement** on **26 January 1950**, the **Indian Constitution** contained only **8 schedules**.
 
• The increase from **8 to 12 schedules** occurred over time through various **Constitutional Amendment Acts** passed by the **Parliament of India** to address evolving administrative and political needs.
 
• The **9th Schedule** was added by the **1st Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1951**.
 
• The **10th Schedule**, known as the **Anti-Defection Law**, was added by the **52nd Constitutional Amendment Act** in **1985**.
 
• The **11th Schedule** and **12th Schedule** were added by the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts** respectively in **1992**, focusing on **Panchayati Raj** and **Municipalities**.

**Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First to Fourth Schedules:**
 
 
• **First Schedule**: Lists the **States and Union Territories** of India and their **territorial jurisdictions**.
 
• **Second Schedule**: Contains provisions relating to the **emoluments, allowances, and privileges** of the **President**, **Governors**, **Speaker of Lok Sabha**, **Judges of Supreme Court**, and **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)**.
 
• **Third Schedule**: Specifies the forms of **Oaths and Affirmations** for **Union Ministers**, **Members of Parliament**, and **Judges**.
 
• **Fourth Schedule**: Details the **allocation of seats** in the **Rajya Sabha** (Council of States) to each **State and Union Territory**.
 
 
 
• **Fifth to Eighth Schedules:**
 
 
• **Fifth Schedule**: Deals with the **administration and control** of **Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• **Sixth Schedule**: Contains special provisions for the **administration of tribal areas** in the states of **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**.
 
• **Seventh Schedule**: Defines the **division of powers** between the Union and States through three lists: **Union List** (currently 100 subjects), **State List** (61 subjects), and **Concurrent List** (52 subjects).
 
• **Eighth Schedule**: Lists the **22 official languages** recognized by the **Indian Constitution**, including **Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, and Sanskrit**.
 
 
 
• **Ninth to Twelfth Schedules:**
 
 
• **Ninth Schedule**: Contains acts and regulations (originally **land reforms**) that are protected from **judicial review**. It was added in **1951**.
 
• **Tenth Schedule**: Contains provisions regarding **disqualification** of members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of **defection**, introduced in **1985**.
 
• **Eleventh Schedule**: Specifies the **29 functional items** or powers of the **Panchayats**, added in **1992**.
 
• **Twelfth Schedule**: Specifies the **18 functional items** or powers of the **Municipalities**, added in **1992**.
 
 

**Important Points__**

 
• The **Indian Constitution** is the **world longest written constitution**. As of **2024**, it has approximately **448 articles** grouped into **25 parts** and **12 schedules**.
 
• The **Drafting Committee**, headed by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, took **2 years, 11 months, and 18 days** to complete the **Constitution**.
 
• The **7th Schedule** is a critical feature of **Indian Federalism**, ensuring a clear **separation of powers** between the **Central Government** and **State Governments**.
 
• The **8th Schedule** originally had **14 languages**; others like **Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali** were added later through **amendments**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Inter-State Council?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resolve disputes between states**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Inter-State Council** is a **constitutional body** established under **Article 263** of the **Constitution of India**. Its primary mandate is to facilitate coordination between the states and the center.

• One of its core functions, as defined in **Article 263(a)**, is **inquiring into and advising upon disputes** which may have arisen between states. This mechanism helps in the peaceful resolution of conflicts through dialogue and recommendation. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***

• The council also investigates and discusses subjects in which the states or the Union have a **common interest**, aiming for better coordination of policy and action.

• The **Inter-State Council** was formally established by a **Presidential Order** on **28 May 1990**, based on the recommendations of the **Sarkaria Commission (1988)**.

• The function of **controlling inter-state trade** is primarily governed by **Articles 301 to 307** of the Constitution and is regulated by **Parliament**, not the Inter-State Council. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• The **allocation of central funds** to the states is the primary responsibility of the **Finance Commission**, a constitutional body constituted under **Article 280** every **five years**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• The **election of the President** of India is conducted by an **Electoral College** as per **Article 54**, consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of the States. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Composition of the Council:** The **Inter-State Council** is chaired by the **Prime Minister**. Its members include the **Chief Ministers** of all states, **Chief Ministers** of Union Territories having a Legislative Assembly, and **Administrators** of UTs not having a Legislative Assembly.

• **Union Cabinet Presence:** The council also includes **six Ministers of Cabinet rank** in the Union Council of Ministers, nominated by the **Prime Minister**.

• **Standing Committee:** A **Standing Committee** of the Inter-State Council was set up in **1996** for continuous consultation and processing of matters for the Council's consideration. It is chaired by the **Union Home Minister**.

• **Nature of Recommendations:** The **Inter-State Council** is a **recommendatory body**. Its advice is not legally binding on the governments, but it carries significant political and administrative weight in a federal setup.

• **Secretariat:** The Council is assisted by a **Secretariat**, which was set up in **1991** and is headed by a **Secretary** to the **Government of India**. Since **2011**, it also functions as the Secretariat for the **Zonal Councils**.

**Important Points__**

• **Article 262 vs Article 263:** While **Article 263** deals with general coordination and dispute inquiry, **Article 262** specifically provides for the **adjudication of disputes** relating to the **waters of inter-state rivers** or river valleys.

• **Sarkaria Commission:** This commission was appointed in **1983** to examine the relationship and balance of power between state and central governments. Its recommendation to make the **Inter-State Council** a permanent body was a landmark in **Indian federalism**.

• **Zonal Councils:** Unlike the Inter-State Council, **Zonal Councils** are **statutory bodies** established under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**. There are currently **five** Zonal Councils (Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern), and the **North-Eastern Council** was created by a separate Act in **1971**.

• **Frequency of Meetings:** According to the **1990 Presidential Order**, the Council should meet at least **three times a year**, though in practice, meetings have been held less frequently.
</ul

questions.question: "Raid" is a commonly used term in which Indian sport?

__
 
• A **Raid** is the primary offensive move in the sport of **Kabaddi**, where a single player from the attacking team, known as the **raider**, runs into the opposing team's half of the court.
 
• The **raider** must continuously chant the word "**Kabaddi**" throughout the duration of the attack without inhaling; this rhythmic chanting is technically referred to as the **cant**.
 
• In professional formats like the **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)**, which was launched in **2014**, each **raid** is restricted to a maximum time limit of **30 seconds**.
 
• The objective of a **raid** is to tag or touch one or more members of the defending team and return safely to the home half. Successfully doing so earns the attacking team **touch points**, while failure to return results in the **raider** being declared "out."
 
• **Kabaddi** is a contact sport with deep roots in **ancient India**, particularly in the state of **Tamil Nadu**. It gained massive international exposure after its introduction as a competitive sport in the **1990 Asian Games** held in **Beijing**.
 
• The sport is governed globally by the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** and in India by the **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)**, which was established in **1972**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Key terminologies include **Offside**, **Dribbling**, **Free Kick**, **Yellow Card**, **Corner Kick**, and **VAR (Video Assistant Referee)**.

• **Hockey**:
 
 
• Field hockey is a widely popular sport in **India** and was historically considered the **national sport** of the country.
 
• Important terms include **Bully**, **Short Corner**, **Penalty Stroke**, **Dribble**, and **Scoop**.
 
• India has won a record **eight Olympic gold medals** in men's hockey, with legends like **Major Dhyan Chand** contributing to its golden era.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Sports**:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **Kabaddi**, a special rule called the **Do-or-Die Raid** occurs when a team has two consecutive **empty raids** (raids where no points are scored). The third raid becomes mandatory for scoring, or the **raider** is automatically out.
 
• The term **Super Tackle** refers to a situation where a defending team with **three or fewer players** successfully pins down a **raider**, earning **2 points** instead of 1.
 
• The **Lona** is an additional **2 points** awarded to a team when they manage to put the entire opposing team "out."

questions.question: A cuboidal block of metal is melted and recast into 12 identical cubes. If the original block had dimensions 24 cm × 6 cm × 6 cm, what is the edge of each cube?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total volume of **cuboidal block** = 24 × 6 × 6 = 864 cm³.

Volume of each of the **12 identical cubes** = 864 ÷ 12 = 72 cm³.

Edge of each cube (a) = √³72 = √³(8 × 9) = 2√³9 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 2√³9 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dimensions of **cuboidal block** = 24 cm × 6 cm × 6 cm

Number of **recast** cubes = 12

**Formula Used:**

Volume of cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

Volume of cube = (Edge)³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d66ef04b875942f37f2e4706242010f4f93a247ae1ba594cb136f7b24376dc80.png] 

⇒ Volume of the **cuboidal block** = 24 × 6 × 6 = 864 cm³

⇒ Let the **edge** of each identical cube be 'a' cm.

⇒ Total volume of 12 cubes = 12 × a³

⇒ Since the block is **melted** and **recast**, total volume remains constant.

⇒ 12 × a³ = 864

⇒ a³ = 864 ÷ 12

⇒ a³ = 72

⇒ a = √³72 = √³(8 × 9)

⇒ a = 2√³9 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 2√³9 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

When a solid is **melted** and **recast** into another shape, the total volume remains the same.

Cube Properties

A cube has 12 edges, 8 vertices, and 6 faces. Volume = a³ and Total Surface Area = 6a².

Cuboid Properties

A cuboid has volume = l × b × h and diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²).</p

questions.question: Two tangents are drawn from an external point P to a circle, touching at points A and B. If the distance from P to the center O is 13 cm, and radius is 5 cm, what is the length of tangent PA?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **tangent PA** is **perpendicular** to the **radius OA** at the point of contact **A**.

This forms a **right-angled triangle OAP** where **OP** is the **hypotenuse**.

Apply the standard **Pythagorean triplet**: (5, 12, 13).

Since **radius (OA) = 5 cm** and **hypotenuse (OP) = 13 cm**, the **tangent (PA)** must be **12 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** of the circle (OA) = 5 cm

Distance of **external point P** from the **center O** (OP) = 13 cm

**Formula Used:**

In a **right-angled triangle**, by **Pythagoras Theorem**: **Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/217087a7add3779c10305b785935350e2de9487b6d653045b9b40d39092866e9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔOAP, ∠OAP = 90° (Radius ⊥ Tangent)

⇒ OP² = OA² + PA²

⇒ 13² = 5² + PA²

⇒ 169 = 25 + PA²

⇒ PA² = 169 − 25

⇒ PA² = 144

⇒ PA = √144

⇒ PA = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Tangent-Radius Property

The **tangent** at any point of a circle is **perpendicular** to the **radius** through the point of contact.

Tangents from an External Point

The lengths of the two **tangents** drawn from an **external point** to a circle are always **equal** (PA = PB).

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) help solve **right-triangle** geometry problems quickly.</p

questions.question: If triangle ABC is congruent to triangle FED, which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In congruence notation Triangle ABC ≅ Triangle FED, the order of letters determines the **corresponding parts**.

Match positions: 1st (A → F), 2nd (B → E), 3rd (C → D).

Side CA consists of the 3rd and 1st vertices, so it must equal the side formed by the 3rd and 1st vertices of the other triangle (DF or FD).

**∴ The correct answer is CA = FD.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Triangle ABC ≅ Triangle FED

**Formula Used:** **CPCT** (Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a2dfebbdadfdd0640079a0ff52cf436a1b888433101e8ba091cbb5913656044.png] 

According to the **CPCT** rule, if two triangles are congruent, their corresponding sides and angles are equal:

⇒ Vertex A corresponds to Vertex F

⇒ Vertex B corresponds to Vertex E

⇒ Vertex C corresponds to Vertex D

Now, let us check the equality of sides:

⇒ AB = FE

⇒ BC = ED

⇒ AC = FD (which can also be written as CA = FD)

Checking the equality of angles:

⇒ ∠A = ∠F

⇒ ∠B = ∠E

⇒ ∠C = ∠D

Comparing these results with the given options, only **CA = FD** is true.

**∴ The correct answer is CA = FD.**

**__Additional Information__**

CPCT Rule

**CPCT** stands for Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles. It states that if two triangles are proved congruent, then all their corresponding parts (sides and angles) are equal.

Criteria for Congruence

Triangles can be proven congruent using five main criteria: **SSS** (Side-Side-Side), **SAS** (Side-Angle-Side), **ASA** (Angle-Side-Angle), **AAS** (Angle-Angle-Side), and **RHS** (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side).

Symbolic Notation

The order of vertices in the congruence statement (e.g., ΔABC ≅ ΔFED) is **mandatory** and must reflect the exact correspondence between the vertices.</p

questions.question: A chord PQ of a circle is equal to its radius. The angle subtended by this chord at a point on the major arc is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Chord PQ** = **Radius** ⇒ **Equilateral Triangle** is formed at the center.

**Central Angle** ∠POQ = 60°.

**Angle at Major Arc** = 1/2 × **Central Angle**.

Angle = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Chord PQ = Radius of the circle.

**Formula:** The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d2cc149080aee5ba4638646e2bd6cbec3a8935f251ce1d26cae6f68464e8d7f8.png] 

⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r.

⇒ In ΔOPQ, OP = OQ = r (Radii of the same circle).

⇒ Given, Chord PQ = r.

⇒ Since OP = OQ = PQ = r, ΔOPQ is an **Equilateral Triangle**.

⇒ ∠POQ = 60° (Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°).

⇒ Let R be a point on the **Major Arc**.

⇒ ∠PRQ = 1/2 × ∠POQ.

⇒ ∠PRQ = 1/2 × 60° = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference is always 90°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°. If the angle at the major arc is θ, the angle at the minor arc is 180° − θ.

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord at any point on the same segment of the circle are equal.</p

questions.question: A positive number exceeds its square root by 132. Find the number given that it is also a multiple of 12.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify the multiple of 12 from the given options: 121, 196, 144, 169.

Only 144 is divisible by 12 (144 ÷ 12 = 12).

Verify the condition: Number − √Number = 132.

144 − √144 = 144 − 12 = 132.

The condition is perfectly satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x − √x = 132

x is a multiple of 12.

**Formula Used:**

Quadratic factorization: y² − y − 132 = 0

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09f3f2be95f5923feea2bc4a674cf4ba889e0e6d302303880c317be16f0deaa2.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let √x = y, then x = y².

⇒ y² − y = 132

⇒ y² − y − 132 = 0

⇒ y² − 12y + 11y − 132 = 0

⇒ y(y − 12) + 11(y − 12) = 0

⇒ (y − 12)(y + 11) = 0

⇒ y = 12 (Since x is a positive number, y cannot be −11)

⇒ x = y² = 12² = 144

⇒ Check multiple: 144 ÷ 12 = 12 (Satisfied)

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 12

A number is divisible by 12 if it is divisible by both 3 and 4. For 144, 1+4+4=9 (divisible by 3) and 44 is divisible by 4.

Quadratic Roots Property

For y² − y − 132 = 0, the product of roots is −132 and the sum of roots is 1. The roots 12 and −11 satisfy this.

Perfect Squares

If a number exceeds its square root by an integer, the number must be a perfect square (e.g., 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...).</p

Consecutive natural numbers always follow the parity pattern (Odd, Even) or (Even, Odd).

This ensures the product is always even, making Assertion (A) correct and justified.

⇒ If n is **Odd**, then n + 1 is **Even** and divisible by 2. Thus, n × (n+1) is divisible by 2.

⇒ In both possible cases, the product contains a factor of 2, ensuring it is always even.

⇒ Reason (R) provides the exact logical explanation for Assertion (A).

**__Additional Information__**

Product of r Consecutive Integers

The product of any r consecutive integers is always divisible by r!. For example, the product of three consecutive numbers is always divisible by 3! = 6.

Sum of Consecutive Numbers

The sum of any two consecutive natural numbers is always **Odd**, as it follows the form n + (n + 1) = 2n + 1.

Parity Multiplication Rules

Even × Even = Even | Even × Odd = Even | Odd × Odd = Odd. Since consecutive numbers always include one even number, their product is always even.</p

questions.question: Which set of numbers includes all others?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The hierarchy of number sets is: **Whole numbers** ⊂ **Integers** ⊂ **Rational numbers** ⊂ **Real numbers**.

**Real numbers** consist of the union of all **Rational** and **Irrational numbers**.

Every **Whole number** is an **Integer**, and every **Integer** is a **Rational number**.

Every **Rational number** is a **Real number**, making it the ultimate superset among the options.

**∴ The correct answer is Real number.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given sets: **Integers**, **Rational numbers**, **Whole numbers**, **Real numbers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1b6c1dd23722917573ef07585f20a8f5b02df609eb1247ed5282029f914e9317.png] 

⇒ **Whole numbers** (W) = {0, 1, 2, 3, ...}

⇒ **Integers** (Z) = {..., −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, ...} ∴ W is a subset of Z.

⇒ **Rational numbers** (Q) = {p/q : p, q are integers, q ≠ 0} ∴ Z is a subset of Q.

⇒ **Real numbers** (R) = Rational ∪ Irrational Numbers ∴ Q is a subset of R.

⇒ By transitivity, R includes Q, Z, and W.

**∴ The correct answer is Real number.**

**__Additional Information__**

Natural Numbers

Counting numbers starting from 1 {1, 2, 3, ...}. They are a subset of **Whole numbers**.

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that cannot be expressed as p/q, such as √2, √3, and π. Together with **Rational numbers**, they form the set of **Real numbers**.

Complex Numbers

The set of numbers in the form a + bi, where a and b are **Real numbers**. This is the largest set and includes **Real numbers** as a subset.</p

questions.question: In a workshop, the ratio of skilled to unskilled workers was **5 : 4**. After a hiring drive, the number of skilled workers increased by **10%**, while the number of unskilled workers increased by **25%**. What is the new ratio of skilled to unskilled workers?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Initial Ratio of **Skilled** to **Unskilled** workers = 5 : 4

New **Skilled** workers = 5 × 110% = 5.5 units

New **Unskilled** workers = 4 × 125% = 5.0 units

New Ratio = 5.5 : 5.0 = 55 : 50 = 11 : 10

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 10.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/759ec674a045ceee1872d767135cb978fcff21dcff4336213762ffd36bacdc53.png] 

Given: Initial ratio of **Skilled** to **Unskilled** workers = 5 : 4.

Formula Used: **New Value** = **Original Value** × (100 + **% Increase**) ÷ 100

⇒ Let the number of **skilled workers** be 500 and **unskilled workers** be 400.

⇒ New number of **skilled workers** = 500 + (10% of 500) = 500 + 50 = 550.

⇒ New number of **unskilled workers** = 400 + (25% of 400) = 400 + 100 = 500.

⇒ **New Ratio** = 550 : 500.

⇒ Dividing both terms by 50: **New Ratio** = 11 : 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 : 10.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change in Ratio

When terms of a ratio a : b increase by x% and y% respectively, the new ratio becomes a(1 + x/100) : b(1 + y/100).

Ratio Multiplier Property

Multiplying both terms of a ratio by the same non-zero constant (k) does not change the ratio (a : b = ka : kb).

Base Value Assumption

questions.question: A student scores 25% more marks in Science than in Math. If he scores 240 marks in Science, how many marks did he score in Math?

**25% more** is equivalent to the fraction **1/4** increase.

Ratio of **Math** marks to **Science** marks = 4 : (4 + 1) = **4 : 5**.

Given **Science** marks (5 units) = **240**.

1 unit = 240 ÷ 5 = **48**.

**Math** marks (4 units) = 4 × 48 = **192**.

**∴ The correct answer is 192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let the marks in **Math** be **x**.

⇒ 240 = x + 0.25x

⇒ 240 = 1.25x

⇒ x = 240 ÷ 1.25

⇒ x = (240 × 100) ÷ 125

⇒ x = 240 × (4 ÷ 5)

⇒ x = 48 × 4

⇒ x = **192**.

**∴ The correct answer is 192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

To find the original value after an increase: **Original = Final Value ÷ (1 + r/100)**, where r is the percentage rate.

Fractional Conversion

Common percentages to fractions: **20% = 1/5**, **25% = 1/4**, **33.33% = 1/3**, **50% = 1/2**.

Base Change Rule

questions.question: Let x and y be angles such that sin(x + y) = 0 and cos(x - y) = 1 . What is the value of the expression: (cos x + cos y)² + (sin x - sin y)² ?

Given sin(x + y) = 0 and cos(x − y) = 1

⇒ x + y = nπ and x − y = 2nπ

⇒ cos(x + y) = 1

⇒ Required value = 2 + 2(1) = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 units.**

Given:

sin(x + y) = 0

cos(x − y) = 1

Expression:

(cos x + cos y)² + (sin x − sin y)²

Formula Used:

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

(a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

⇒ (cos x + cos y)²

⇒ = cos²x + cos²y + 2cos x cos y

⇒ (sin x − sin y)²

⇒ = sin²x + sin²y − 2sin x sin y

⇒ Adding both:

⇒ cos²x + sin²x + cos²y + sin²y + 2(cos x cos y − sin x sin y)

⇒ x + y = 0, π, 2π ...

⇒ Taking principal value, cos(x + y) = 1

⇒ Required value = 2 + 2(1)

⇒ = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4 units.**

Trigonometric Identity

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 is the most frequently used trigonometric identity.

Cosine Addition Formula

General Solution of sin θ = 0

If sin θ = 0, then θ = nπ where n is an integer.

If cos θ = 1, then θ = 2nπ where n is an integer.

questions.question: The time taken for a train to pass a pole is 18 seconds, while it takes 33 seconds to cross a bridge measuring 300 meters. Calculate the length of the train.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra time taken to cross the bridge = 33 − 18 = 15 seconds.

This extra 15 seconds is the time required to cover the bridge length of 300 meters.

Speed of the train = 300 ÷ 15 = 20 m/s.

Length of the train = Speed × Time to cross pole = 20 × 18 = 360 meters.

**∴ The correct answer is 360 meters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to cross pole = 18 s

Time to cross bridge = 33 s

Length of bridge = 300 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/946ac04cc4284ab344970684b508b71c21860eee4085b3cd0cc30312bd763418.png] 

Let the length of the train be L meters.

⇒ Speed of train = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Speed = L ÷ 18 (while crossing the pole)

⇒ Speed = (L + 300) ÷ 33 (while crossing the bridge)

Equating the speed in both cases:

⇒ L ÷ 18 = (L + 300) ÷ 33

⇒ 33 × L = 18 × (L + 300)

⇒ 33L = 18L + 5400

⇒ 33L − 18L = 5400

⇒ 15L = 5400

⇒ L = 5400 ÷ 15

⇒ L = 360 meters

**∴ The correct answer is 360 meters.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a point object (pole, man, tree), distance = length of train. When it crosses a platform, bridge, or another stationary train, distance = length of train + length of the object.

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: Two equal sums are lent at 6% and 9% simple interest per annum respectively. The interest received on both sums after 4 years differs by ₹150. Find each sum.

Sum = 12.5 × 100 = ₹1250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1250.**

⇒ (36P/100) − (24P/100) = 150

⇒ 12P/100 = 150

⇒ 12P = 150 × 100

⇒ P = 15000 ÷ 12

⇒ P = 1250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1250.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the **line of sight** with the horizontal when the object being viewed is **above** the horizontal level.

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

For a 30° angle, tan 30° = 1 / √3. For a 60° angle, tan 60° = √3.

Isosceles Right Triangle Property
